problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(2,1,-3)$ and is  perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+t \\ y=2-t \\ z=3+2t.\end{aligned}
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Vector Equation of a Plane

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of the Plane Perpendicular to a Given Straight Line
examples.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(\sqrt{2},0,-5)$ and is perpendicular to the line

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3 \\ y=-1+\sqrt{3}t \\ z=5-t.\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $Q$ is $\mathbf{q}=\langle \sqrt{2},0,-5 \rangle.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083941/assets/3c1e2e4034bcbc860f548935ca7305bc8f141c56ba14f821fd1aa6cb2b53f8d9.png)

The direction vector of the line is $\mathbf{v}=\langle  0 , \sqrt{3} , -1\rangle,$ so a normal vector to the plane is 

$$
\mathbf{n}=\mathbf{v}=\langle  0 , \sqrt{3} , -1 \rangle.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,\sqrt{3},-1⟩ & =⟨\sqrt{2},0,-5⟩\cdot ⟨0,\sqrt{3},-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,\sqrt{3},-1⟩ & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩=7.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩=7$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-3,1,-2⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-3,1,-2⟩ & =0 \\ -3{t}_{1}+{t}_{2}-2{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & =3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,3{t}_{1}+2{t}_{3},\,{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{3}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{3}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=2.$
